rationale.complete: Round 1 done: pre-registered predictions, 30k Jev labels with two blind validation sets, synthetic validation at the real reply graphs (S1-S6), four periods with verdicts, a calibrated null for the detector, and a #34 confirmatory script with dry run. Not done: a second labeller or rater, the holdout run, contested periods, signed reply dynamics. Round 1c (2026-10-04): DQ2 ledger-visible pairs, DQ10 validated disagreement flag with the labeller's precision and recall in every null, DQ6 ground truth, synthetic power on the real structures, all primary predictions re-tested; #34 re-freeze proposed.
rationale.faithfulness: Clear but partial: the positive control passes strongly (beats team permutation, agent fields and topic; teams recovered 7/10), but the hypothesis' general claim fails where conflict is not assigned (#51 roles, #26 ballots), and the per-pair and faction nulls needed post-hoc calibration. Round 1c: #12 contrast holds as disagreement on the merits (33/74 vs 0/60; stress null p 0.001); #40 false-alarm clause now passes; #51 failure now has a stated reach (rivals excluded at +2, opposed at +3 log-odds); governance-friction lead not replicated.
rationale.usefulness: A cheap detector of assigned or explicit sides with measured accuracy and a calibrated false-alarm rate that an operator can run on chat logs. Payoff is limited because LLM swarms rarely produce stance conflict, Jev's negative calls are imprecise, and the saboteur use case is untested (holdout).

one_line: A validated disagreement flag recovers assigned debate conflict that topic misses (33/74 vs 0/60 replies) and stays quiet elsewhere; rivals, opposed roles and voters show no excess disagreement.
